newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive says currency hits 9-mo sales.
newsitem.headline: Incentive says currency hits 9-mo sales.

text.p: Incentive AB, the Swedish industrial group whose core business is medical technology supplier Gambro, on Wednesday said a stronger crown slashed its nine-month sales but earnings still rose.
Sales totalled 14.22 billion crowns ($2.14 billion) in the first nine months of 1996, down from 17.79 billion.
However Incentive said it was hit by negative currency effects which wiped 160 million crowns off earnings of 1.38 billion crowns in the nine months to September 30.
"Given the currency group structure and adjusted for currency effect sales rose 14 percent," the company said in its nine month report.
The group's profit after financial items for its own operations rose to 3.14 billion crowns from 1.96 billion, but a one-off gain of 2.57 billion crowns lifted this result.

The one-off capital gain was from the sale of shareholdings and companies and the amortization of goodwill from the Gambro purchase that totalled 361 million crowns compared to 114 million in the same 1995 period.

In the third quarter it completed the sale of power company Skandinaviska Elverk AB (SEV) for a capital gain of 1.9 billion crowns and a reduction of net debt by 5.9 billion, saying it brought the group closer to its aim of focusing operations.

"This marked yet another decisive step in Incentive's restructuring. At the same time, this divestment substantially strengthened the group's financial position," Incentive said in its nine month result statement.
Sales in Incentive's medical technology area rose to 8.03 billion crowns from 7.62 billion, but would have risen nine percent adjusted for currency effects and acqusitions.
Incentive said in the third quarter sales in Europe stayed weak but those in the U.S. and Asia developed favourably.
Sales in Asia jumped 30 percent and now make up 14 percent of total sales, compared to 11 percent a year ago. ($ = 6.636 Swedish Crowns)
